top_findings.title: No MCP server layer — the central deliverable is absent
top_findings.evidence: grep -niE 'import mcp|from mcp|fastmcp|Server\(|@tool|@mcp|register_tool|list_tools|call_tool|stdio_server' across all 8 *.py returns nothing; requirements.txt:2 lists 'mcp>=1.0.0' but it is never imported; no server entrypoint (no def main / mcp.run); every module is a plain query-engine class. test_brazilian_soccer.py:10-15 imports the engine classes directly rather than through any MCP interface.
top_findings.suggestion: Add a server module that instantiates FastMCP (or mcp.server.Server), registers each query-engine method as a @tool, and exposes a stdio entrypoint.

top_findings.title: Season standings computed from only the 20 most-recent matches
top_findings.evidence: competition_queries.py:28 get_competition_standings calls self.match_engine.find_matches(competition=..., season=...) with no limit; find_matches (match_queries.py:23) defaults limit=20 and match_queries.py:73 does sort_values('datetime', ascending=False).head(limit), truncating a ~38-match Brasileirao season to 20 rows. get_champion (competition_queries.py:110-113) reads standings[0] off this truncated table, so points/positions and the champion are wrong.
top_findings.suggestion: Pass an unbounded limit (e.g. limit=None handled to skip .head) from all season-aggregation call sites.

top_findings.title: Team W/L/D and goals aggregated over only 20 matches
top_findings.evidence: team_queries.py:29 get_team_statistics calls find_matches(team1=..., competition=..., season=...) with no limit; the default limit=20 (match_queries.py:23,73) caps the sample, so wins/draws/losses/goals_for/goals_against/points (team_queries.py:80-95) reflect only the 20 most-recent matches, not the full season.
top_findings.suggestion: Compute team statistics over the full filtered match set, not the 20-row default window.
